lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The Coastal Marine Services role should take up only one line.
items.because: It is unrelated to the product and operations story, but its two bullets give it too much space.

items.says: The Experience entries are not in newest-first order: Crestline appears above the newer Harbor Payments role.
items.because: The ordering obscures which experience is more recent.

items.says: Education appears above Experience despite the substantial professional history.
items.because: The current order gives education priority over several years of experience and later product work.

items.says: The bullet gives no outcome from the maintenance or inspections.
“Maintained” does not say what work was performed on the hydraulic winch systems.
The scorecard and meeting bullet describes duties without stating what they changed.
items.because: It shows responsibility and meeting purpose, but not a decision or operational improvement the work enabled.

items.says: “New” adds no useful information to “layout.”
The 1,800-hour result is buried after a long list of methods and responsibilities.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the bullet’s clearest impact.

items.says: The stack of details is difficult to scan, and “taking over vendor negotiations” names a responsibility rather than a specific action or outcome.
The RICE bullet does not name the initiative it led to prioritizing.
items.because: A reader can see the framework used, but not the product decision it influenced.

items.says: The RICE and Reach explanation uses jargon and a cumbersome description of the criterion.
The bullet does not name the selected priority, and its long method list comes before the decision.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what product decision the research and business case drove.

items.says: The loss analysis gives no estimate or comparison to show the scale of the opportunity.
items.because: Without an estimate, a reader cannot judge the opportunity supporting the roadmap decision.

items.says: Session randomization does not by itself establish a customer-level effect, and the lift is described unclearly.
items.because: It estimates a session-level effect; customers with multiple sessions could encounter both versions.

items.says: The bullet repeats the checkout A/B test and five-point lift already reported in the preceding bullet.
items.because: The duplication makes the achievement look repeated rather than broader.

items.says: “Who funded the rollout” makes the connection between the presentation and funding indirect.
“That would have been thrown away” repeats the idea conveyed by “surplus-food.”
The change from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is a 187.5% increase, not 150%.
items.because: The increase is 750 users over a baseline of 400.

items.says: The weekly-active-user increase has no timeframe.
The fill rate rose by 20 percentage points, not by 20% as a relative increase.
items.because: The stated rates move from 75% to 95%, a difference of 20 percentage points.

items.says: “Sized a $2.4M annual saving” could be read as realized savings although it came from a model.
items.because: A reader needs to know whether the amount is a forecast or an outcome already achieved.

items.says: The pilot funding is reported here and again in the presentation bullet.
items.because: Repeating the result makes the entry look less varied and takes space from the modeled savings estimate.

items.says: The intake bullet does not say what improved after the form was shortened.
The passive wording makes it unclear who mapped patient intake and shortened the form.
